svg.text: E Sub-mechanisms (2) — preparation tools that fit the wash
Each panel loops on its own. Every tool is a plain shape that falls apart or never needs a joint in the food zone.
source: E-cleaning-first.md section 6
S11 apron roller: see E-zwei-bahnen
S3 Spike lathe

g.text: floating Y-peeler, 3–5 N, pole to pole

svg.text: Potato between spike and cup; 8–12 s each. Knife tops and tails;
dicing: 24 meridian cuts (15° index), then slices across.
Feasibility H peeling, M dicing
S9 Flexure-iris peeler
Carrot pushed point first through 6 standard peeler blades,
turned 30° and pushed back; 5 s per carrot. No hinge, no spring.
Feasibility M (crevice-free blade weld)
S15 Water jet as the peeler

g.text: closed tub, water recirculated through a strainer

svg.text: Pressure-washer pump 1.4 kW, 6 L/min: thin skins (carrot, new potato,
ginger) strip off; ~1.5 L and 15 s per piece. No tool to clean.
Feasibility L–M (loud, aerosol); a one-day test
S16 Steam-slip onion peeling

g.text: ram pushes it through the ring
skin and first layer stay behind

svg.text: Cook's trick for pearl onions; steam from the cooking module.
The outer layer is slightly cooked — irrelevant when sweated.
Feasibility M
S17 Decap, do not crack
Shell stays in two whole pieces: far fewer fragments than
an equator crack. Yolk must pass the Ø32 opening intact.
Feasibility M
S6 Freeze-plate gripper

g.text: plate at −10 °C freezes the moisture film

svg.text: Fish fillet, meat slice, dough sheet held by 1–2 s of freezing.
The gripper is a flat plate — the easiest shape to clean.
Feasibility M; fails on dry or floured surfaces
